story_type: cruise ship hoist after a night of fog, swimmer rides the cable down to the top deck
hook: She waited all night on this ship while fog kept help away.
narration: A woman on this cruise ship had a stroke, and fog kept help away all night.
The Carnival Pride was fifteen miles east of Charleston, South Carolina.
The Coast Guard got the call at six twenty seven in the evening. Heavy fog that night pushed the launch to seven the next morning.
Then an MH-65 Dolphin from Air Station Savannah lowered its rescue swimmer toward the ship.
There is nowhere for a helicopter to land on most cruise ships, so everything rides the cable. The swimmer, the basket, and the patient.
Two people came up from the deck: the woman, and a nurse from the ship.
A litter rose past the top deck and swung in toward the cabin door.
Last, the swimmer rode the cable back up over open water.
outcome: Both were flown to Roper St. Francis Hospital, and the woman was reported to be in stable condition.
title: Fog kept her waiting all night at sea
description:
A Coast Guard Air Station Savannah MH-65 Dolphin crew hoisted a woman and a nurse from the cruise ship Carnival Pride 15 miles east of Charleston, South Carolina, on Jan. 30, 2018, after heavy fog delayed the launch overnight.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 1st Class Luke Clayton, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/582149/coast-guard-medevacs-cruise-ship-passenger-15-miles-east-charleston

facts.claim: Woman medevaced from the Carnival Pride 15 miles east of Charleston
facts.source_quote: Coast Guard crews medevaced a 46-year-old woman Tuesday from the cruise ship Carnival Pride 15 miles east of Charleston.
The woman was reported to have suffered a stroke.

facts.claim: Call at 6:27 p.m., launch at 7 a.m. because of heavy fog, MH-65 from Air Station Savannah
facts.source_quote: Coast Guard Sector Charleston watchstanders received notification at 6:27 p.m. Monday and launched a Coast Guard Air Station Savannah MH-65 Dolphin rescue helicopter crew at 7 a.m. due to low visibility from heavy fog Monday night.

facts.claim: Woman and a nurse hoisted, taken to Roper St. Francis Hospital, stable
facts.source_quote: The woman and a nurse were hoisted and taken to Roper St. Francis Hospital at 8:13 a.m. The woman was reported to be in stable condition.
